extracted.intended_audience: civil and mechanical engineers, architects, builders, and sanitary officers (late-19th-century practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical technical and sanitary guidance for designing and constructing locomotives, tunnels, dams, canals, and healthy dwelling houses, including dimensional specifications, material/assembly methods, and sanitary building practices. The page contains workmanship guidance, numerical design proportions, and construction procedures intended for practicing engineers and architects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locomotive tractive_force_per_effective_piston_pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Tractive force which the engine is capable of exerting amounts to (diameter^2 x stroke) / 46 = lb. for each pound of effective pressure per square inch on the pistons (example given: (20.48² x 24) / 46 = 218.4 lb. per lb./sq.in.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the piston diameter and stroke together with wheel diameter in the formula to estimate tractive force; note that high tractive force requires corresponding adhesive weight (engine weight available for adhesion). Example: mean effective pressure of ~102½ lb./sq.in. would exert a pull of 10 tons given the calculated tractive force and engine weight (44 tons empty, 51 tons in working order).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cylinder_and_wheel_proportions_affecting_tractive_power
rubrics_metrics.description: Cylinder dimensions (diameter and stroke) and coupled wheel diameter directly determine tractive force (illustrated by engine with outside cylinders 20.48 in. diameter, 24 in. stroke, coupled wheels 3 ft. 10 in.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing locomotive power, choose cylinder diameter and stroke in relation to wheel diameter to obtain required tractive force; ensure engine weight supplies adhesion to utilize cylinder power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locomotive_frame_construction_and_staying
rubrics_metrics.description: Frames should be deep and heavy (example: 1 3/8 in. thick) and stayed by substantial box framing at smokebox end, cast-iron footplate at rear end, and intermediate plate stays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure cylinders to frames and provide robust stays to resist loads; use adjusting wedges on axle box guides and substantial frame members to maintain alignment and durability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axle_bearings_dimensions_and_axle_spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Axle bearings specified as 7.87 in. diameter by 9.45 in. long; axles spaced at equal distances (example: 4 ft. 3.1 in. apart) giving a total wheel base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize axle bearings dimensions and maintain equal axle spacing for balanced wheelbase and consistent bearing loads; provide uniformity across axles for maintenance and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spring_arrangement_and_trailing_axle_compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use springs above axle boxes with compensating beams for coupled axles; for trailing axle, employ a bell-crank lever arrangement transmitting load to a transverse spring pivoted to transverse stays so the spring can be kept clear of the firebox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt compensating beams for even load distribution and a trailing-axle spring arrangement that allows full-width firebox between frames; ensure trailing wheels can be fitted with brakes as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve_motion_and_clearance_of_axles
rubrics_metrics.description: Valve motion example: Gooch (stationary link) type with radius rods cranked to clear the leading axle and eccentric rods bent to clear the second axle; piston rods extended through front cylinder covers and enlarged where they enter crossheads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design valve motion such that link/gearing clear axles and other obstructions; make gland and piston entries serviceable (e.g., glands made in halves) and provide adequate clearances in motion layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiler_design_working_pressure_and_dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Boiler constructed for a working pressure of 147 lb. per square inch; barrel diameter, plate thickness, firebox shape and stays are specified (example: barrel 60.4 in. diameter, plates 0.65 in. thick; firebox of copper with crown stayed directly to casing crown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify boiler working pressure and ensure barrel and firebox dimensions, plate thicknesses, stays and transverse stays to resist spreading; include dome for regulator and consider exhaust nozzle closure for reversing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boiler_heating_surface_and_firegrate_area_ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Key proportions given: heating surface — Tubes 1598.5 sq.ft., Firebox 102.5 sq.ft., total 1701.0 sq.ft.; firegrate area 23.3 sq.ft.; ratios: firegrate area to heating surface 1:73, flue area through tubes to firegrate area 1:6.7, least sectional area of chimney to firegrate area 1:17.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use heating surface and grate area ratios to assess boiler steaming capacity; the comparatively small chimney-to-grate area was chosen to obtain strong draught at low running speeds — adjust these ratios to intended operating speed and draft conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use_of_mechanized_boring_for_tunnel_excavation_rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacing manual pick-and-shovel with a Beaumont boring machine increases advance rate from about ten yards per week to fifty yards per week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ mechanized boring where feasible to greatly increase excavation progress; select tunnelling machinery appropriate to geology and tunnel cross-section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tunnel_drainage_headings_and_pumping_capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Drainage headings act as reservoirs draining water from the main tunnel to both river sides where pumps discharge it. Example pump sets: Liverpool shafts discharge 6,100 gallons per minute, Birkenhead 5,040 gallons per minute; additional 40 in. pumps provided for contingency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design drainage headings and pumping installations to handle worst-case inflows; provide redundancy and sufficient capacity to avoid delays from pump failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tunnel_lining_and_thickness_near_river
rubrics_metrics.description: Tunnel lined throughout with solid brickwork: ordinary sections 18 inches thick (two layers blue + two red brick); near the river increased to six rings of brick (three blue + three red); Portland cement layer for added stability; about 22 yards of brickwork in every yard forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide robust brick lining and cement backing where external loads or water exposure are severe; increase lining thickness towards river or weak ground and account for high quantities of brickwork per yard of advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tunnel_and_station_dimensions_and_form
rubrics_metrics.description: Main tunnel dimensions example: 26 ft. wide and 21 ft. high; drainage heading 7 ft. diameter; main tunnel form is semicircular with arch and side/base radii specified in text; underground stations 400 ft long, 51 ft wide, and 32 ft high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine tunnel dimensions and cross-sectional shape to accommodate intended traffic and services; include stations with adequate platform and headroom dimensions and provide safety niches at intervals (example: 18 in. depth at every 45 ft. on alternate sides).

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety_niches_and_worker_provisions_in_tunnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety niches of 18 in. depth are placed at every 45 ft. on alternate sides for platelayers' safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate regular safety recesses and access provisions for emergency refuge and maintenance during tunnelling and operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dam_design_requirements_for_large_flowing_river
rubrics_metrics.description: Dam required to be 'as near perfectly tight as possible' and always submerged; crest depth intended 2.50 ft in low water and about 10 ft in high water; design must account for extreme flows (example: Ottawa River flows from 26,000 cu.ft./s in extreme low to 190,000 cu.ft./s in highest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large rivers provide dam height to achieve required upstream water depths for navigation while ensuring watertightness; design for seasonal extremes and limited working windows during low water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary_works_and_sequence_to_break_current_and_build_dam
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct temporary structures immediately above dam site in sections to break the current (timber sills bolted to rock, cribs sunk, platforms built across river), then erect flat dam structure and fill with stone; drill and bolt cribs into rock and sheet upstream sides with tamarack planking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage construction: use sills & cribs to establish working platform, clean rock bottom by divers, bolt timberwork into plugs, build continuous platform, then construct superstructure and fill; adapt temporary works to depth and current conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method_of_closing_sluices_and_gates_for_dam_completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Sluices closed by timber gates 10 in. thick hung on strong wooden hinges; gates laid back on face of dam and then turned over into place so the current carries them into position (closing delicate and potentially dangerous operation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare gates and hinge arrangements to allow remote or controlled closure by using river current; expect delicate operations and provide for replacement/filling of displaced gates if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timber_slide_design_for_timber_passage
rubrics_metrics.description: Timber slide formed by parallel piers about 600 ft long up and down stream, 28 ft apart, with timber bottom whose top at upper end is 3 ft below crest of dam; includes stop logs and machinery to control water and guide booms extending about half a mile upstream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design timber slides with adequate length, piers spacing, control stop logs and machinery; provide approach guide booms for safe timber passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canal_and_lock_dimensions_and_lift_distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Locks required: 200 ft long, 45 ft wide, with not less than 9 ft of water on the sills at lowest water; lock walls example: 29 ft high (lower) and 31 ft (upper), 10 to 12 ft thick at bottom; rise overcome by two locks is 16 ft (distribution varies with water level).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify locks sized for anticipated vessels and minimum water levels; construct strong masonry lock walls and oak miter sills; design lift distribution considering seasonal level variations so miter sills maintain sufficient depth in all conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embankment_and_pier_protection_against_ice_and_erosion
rubrics_metrics.description: Embankments backed by a puddle wall (three feet thick) and rubble masonry on canal side, crib-work on river side filled with earth; outer slope protected with riprap of large bowlders to resist moving spring ice; timber piers provided (examples: upper pier 800 ft long, lower 300 ft).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct embankments in layers (earth layers not more than one foot thick), provide puddle walls and crib-work where needed, and use riprap to resist ice damage. Build piers to required heights and widths for navigation and protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations_and_subsoil_treatment_for_dwellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not leave top soil enclosed within outer walls; often cover subsoil with a layer of cement concrete and at times asphalt on the concrete; subsoil that is damp or porous can cause moisture rise or percolation of offensive matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select healthy localities where possible; improve site by planting/subdrainage; when building, remove or isolate topsoil from beneath foundations and use damp-proof layers (concrete/asphalt) to prevent rising moisture and contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellar_design_and_sanitary_requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cellars are often abominations; if cellars are necessary they should be constructed with damp-proof walls and floors, light should be freely admitted, every part must be well ventilated, and above all, no drain of any description should be taken in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cellars when possible. Where used, ensure cellars are dry, well-lit, well-ventilated, and do not act as receptacles for drains which may introduce contamination. Floors can be kept clean with minimal water if properly sealed, making special drains unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damp_course_over_whole_of_walls_internal_and_external
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a good damp course over the whole of the walls, internal as well as external; omission (often to save cost) leads to rising damp and coldness within houses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include damp-proof courses throughout all internal and external walls (not just outer walls), particularly in areas that are not on dry ground; prioritize sanitary durability over superficial ornamentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance_of_workmanship_and_supervision_in_sanitary_details
rubrics_metrics.description: Architects need trustworthy, careful workmen; many sanitary defects arise because architect's instructions are not carried out or are covered up by careless/ignorant workmen, leading to unsanitary conditions discovered only after illness or death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear, detailed sanitary specifications and active supervision on site; select competent contractors and workmanship to implement damp-proofing, drainage, ventilation and other critical details so that the planned sanitary measures are effective long-term.
